frequency_question: How often does the Department of Education actually complete a full formal revocation of an established accreditor's national recognition within a given administrative term?
membership_rule: Includes any formal administrative action initiated or finalized by the U.S. Department of Education to strip an agency of its recognized status as an accreditor; excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probation terms that did not result in termination.
window: 1992 to present (Modern Higher Education Act reauthorization framework)

cases.name: American Bar Association (Prior 1995-1996 antitrust consent decree and review)

coverage_note: 3 major contested episodes named; estimated 4 total high-stakes challenges where termination was actively weighed.
known_gaps: Lower-profile programmatic accreditors sometimes face quiet terminations or renewals under conditions not publicly equivalent to a high-stakes showdown with a major entity like the ABA.
skeleton: Total formal recognition termination attempts against major national/professional accreditors under the HEA framework since 1992.
multiplier: 2 successful revocations out of approximately 4 major contested review processes over three decades.
validity_reason: Statutory framework governing institutional accreditation under the Higher Education Act remains stable across multiple presidential administrations.
